title:
MY SUPPORT
CIRCLE
intro_quote: “Who could you lean on when things feel difficult?”
intro_desc: Support can look different for everyone. It might be someone you talk to, someone you spend time with, or someone who simply listens.
step_1_desc: You don’t need someone you talk to every day. Think of people who make you feel safe, heard, or supported.
step_2_title:
WHAT KIND OF
SUPPORT FEELS RIGHT?
step_2_desc: When things are difficult, what would you most want from someone?
step_3_empty_desc: Knowing that support is an option can still be useful.
step_4_desc: What feels like the easiest way for you to reach out?

plans.send_message_sentence: When things feel difficult, I can start by sending a message to someone I trust.
plans.make_call_sentence: When things feel difficult, I can start by calling someone I trust.
plans.meet_in_person_sentence: When things feel difficult, I can reach out to meet someone in person.
plans.spend_time_sentence: When things feel difficult, I can share quiet time or an activity with someone.
plans.professional_first_sentence: When things feel difficult, reaching out to a structured professional feels best for me.
plans.not_ready_yet_sentence: You don’t have to reach out before you’re ready. Knowing your options is still a meaningful first step.

completion.title:
YOU’VE BUILT
YOUR CIRCLE
completion.text_1: Support doesn’t always mean having the right words.
completion.text_2: Sometimes the first step is simply knowing who you could turn to.
completion.takeaway_quote: “Knowing where you can turn is a form of preparation.”
